headline: 生産, “production”, is traced to Literary Chinese 生產, glossed “procreation; reproduction; making a living; livelihood”.
チャイム is the English word “chime” in katakana.
運, “fortune, luck”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC hjunH).
オーバー covers “overcoat” and “over, exceeding”, and the source traces it to English “over”.
案, “plan, scheme, proposal”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC 'anH).
ステーキ is borrowed from English “steak”.
襖, “sliding screen”, is a compound of 臥す (fusu) plus 間 (ma).
バケツ is the English word “bucket” in katakana.
ヘリコプター is borrowed from English “helicopter”.
少し, “little, few”, is from Old Japanese and possibly related to 少ない (sukunai).
ベルト, “belt for western clothes”, is the English word “belt” in katakana.
繋がり is the continuative stem of the verb 繋がる (tsunagaru, “to be connected”).
バター is borrowed from English “butter”.
炒める, “to stir-fry”, comes from the earlier verb 炒む (itamu).
ゴール is borrowed from English “goal”.
ケーキ is borrowed from English “cake”.
まさか is first attested in the Man'yōshū of 759, and the source lists several theories of its derivation.
ノート, “notebook”, is borrowed from English “note”.
祝い, “celebration”, is the continuative stem of the verb 祝う (iwau, “to celebrate”).
ダイヤル is borrowed from English “dial”.
これから is literally “[starting] from this”.
サービス is borrowed from English “service”.
作, “a work, a harvest”, is from Middle Chinese 作 (tsak, “to do, to work”).
パーセント is borrowed from English “percent”.
デザイン is the English word “design” in katakana.
飢える came from the classical verb 飢う (uu), with a sound path from /uwu/ to /ueru/.
ポケット is the English word “pocket” in katakana.
世話 is believed to derive from 忙しい (sewashii, “busy”), and its kanji are ateji.
ダンス is borrowed from English “dance”.
そんな is a contraction of その様な (sono yō na).
ジーンズ is the English word “jeans” in katakana.
